claims.text: Single-phase ZrB2 has strong Zr–B and B–B bonds.
Adding 2–5 wt% SiC enables ZrB2 densification by spark plasma sintering at approximately 1700 °C.
SiC addition engineers the grain boundaries of ZrB2.
Processing SiC-modified ZrB2 produces a Si-rich intergranular phase along ZrB2 grain boundaries.
The Si-rich intergranular phase may be an in situ generated borosilicate glass.
SiC acts as a sintering aid that promotes densification at lower temperatures.
SiC partially reacts during sintering and supplies silicon that stabilizes ZrB2 grain boundaries.
The Si-rich grain-boundary phase limits oxygen ingress during high-temperature exposure.
The Si-rich grain-boundary phase impedes liquid plating-metal penetration.
Limiting oxygen and liquid-metal ingress preserves the strength and structural integrity of ZrB2.
SiC-modified ZrB2 processed at approximately 1700 °C will have similar or improved mechanical strength and structural integrity relative to single-phase ZrB2 processed above 2300 °C.
SiC-modified ZrB2 will have better oxidation resistance than single-phase high-temperature-processed ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
SiC-modified ZrB2 will be less susceptible to liquid plating-metal corrosion than single-phase high-temperature-processed ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
Single-phase ZrB2 processed above 2300 °C achieves high intrinsic strength.
Single-phase ZrB2 processed above 2300 °C is difficult to manufacture with controlled microstructures.
Historical ZrB2 methods below 1700 °C produce inadequate oxidation and corrosion performance.
The proposed protective behavior applies when SiC content is below about 5 wt% and sintering is performed near 1700 °C.
The proposed protection remains effective up to approximately 1200 °C in oxidizing and liquid-plating environments.

contradictions.description: The baseline describes historical lower-temperature methods as below 1700 °C, whereas the proposed approximately 1700 °C process is itself presented as reduced-temperature processing; the meaning of the lower-temperature comparison class is therefore inconsistent or insufficiently defined.
